title: Multi-calendar discovery and meeting-prep RI quality defect
source: ChatGPT / live RB meeting-prep session summary
category: Connector discovery / onboarding readiness / meeting prep quality
summary: Todd asked RB to prep for afternoon meetings. The assistant initially failed to discover the correct calendar/account context, assumed no meetings existed from an empty lookup, required manual account specification, and then produced useful but not canonical Chief-of-Staff meeting prep.
observed_issue: RB behaved like a helpful strategist with partial calendar access, not like a relationship operating system with source inventory, connector confidence, and meeting-prep orchestration.

steps.label: User requested afternoon meeting prep
steps.user_prompt: lets prep for our meetings this afternoon.
steps.expected_behavior: Check connected calendars, recognize multi-account ambiguity if the default calendar is empty, enumerate accessible calendars, search likely business calendars, and present source confidence before producing prep.
steps.observed_behavior: Initial calendar lookup returned empty. The assistant treated that as no meetings rather than a source-discovery failure or account-selection ambiguity.

steps.label: User had to specify business account
steps.user_action: Todd had to specify todd@bridgepointops.com and troubleshoot connector/calendar visibility.
steps.expected_behavior: No meetings found on the default calendar. Additional Google accounts may exist but are not currently enumerated. Attempting accessible calendar discovery...
steps.observed_issue: Calendar source inventory and fallback search behavior were missing from the conversational path.

steps.label: Meeting prep generated
observed_strengths: Good adoption, rollout, franchisee reality, and anti-hype framing.
Correct risk recognition around unpaid consulting drift, pick-your-brain traps, intro harvesting, and free GTM strategy extraction.
observed_gaps: Did not review prior messages or calendar history.
Did not examine shared contacts or referral patterns.
Did not assess reciprocity, trust trajectory, relationship stage, or strategic value.
Did not define desired outcomes, success criteria, next-step options, or disqualification triggers.
Did not judge whether the relationship should be active pursuit, nurture, monitor, low-priority, or avoid.
steps.observed_issue: Prep was good advisory prose, not evidence-backed RI-driven CoS prep.

current_architecture_notes.multi_account_manifest: system/inbox/accounts.yaml is documented as the multi-account manifest.
current_architecture_notes.calendar_aggregation: rb_core.load_calendar() aggregates calendar.<account_id>.json files across enabled accounts.
current_architecture_notes.refresh_wrapper: refresh_sources.py --calendar can normalize per-account raw calendar files and prints missing-input instructions.
current_architecture_notes.daily_brief_support: Daily brief has a Meeting Prep & Deliverables section.
current_architecture_notes.remaining_gap: RB lacks a conversational source-readiness layer that can enumerate connected accounts/calendars, score confidence, detect missing business calendars, and tell the user whether prep is grounded or under-instrumented before generating advice.

expected_source_readiness_behavior: Enumerate accessible calendars and Gmail identities.
Identify default, personal, business, and stale/missing feeds.
Search all likely business calendars before declaring no meetings.
Report source confidence and missing connectors.
Ask to connect additional calendars only after automatic discovery fails.
Maintain a startup/system-readiness score that includes calendar/Gmail visibility.

source_proof: Email evidence searched and freshness state.
LinkedIn/social evidence searched and freshness state.
time_allocation_judgment: Active pursuit / nurture / monitor / low-priority / avoid.

defects.title: Empty default calendar result overtrusted
defects.description: RB treated an empty calendar lookup as no meetings instead of detecting account ambiguity or source-inventory uncertainty.
defects.recommendation: Calendar-aware prompts must run a source-discovery/readiness check before concluding no events exist.

defects.title: Multi-account setup guidance missing
defects.description: The user had to discover and name the business calendar manually. RB should guide users through connecting multiple Gmail/calendar accounts and validating visibility.
defects.recommendation: Add multi-account onboarding checklist, connector heartbeat validation, and source-readiness scoring.

defects.title: Meeting prep lacked real relationship intelligence
defects.description: The prep inferred from titles and general context but did not prove it searched email, LinkedIn, prior interactions, shared contacts, active threads, loop state, or source freshness.
defects.recommendation: Meeting prep must include source proof and label under-instrumented areas explicitly.

defects.title: No why-this-matters ranking
defects.description: The prep did not explicitly rank strategic upside, risk, time investment, or likelihood of opportunity.
defects.recommendation: Add a why_this_meeting_matters section with priority, upside, risk, and recommended posture.

defects.title: Missing outcome strategy
defects.description: The prep focused on conversation flow, but not desired next step, success criteria, conversion target, escalation path, post-meeting actions, or disqualification triggers.
defects.recommendation: Canonical meeting prep should end with outcome strategy and post-meeting orchestration.

raw_text: Test Assessment — Multi-Calendar Access + Meeting Prep Quality. Multi-calendar setup was eventually functional but not executive-grade. Meeting prep was strategically intelligent but lacked actual RI, evidence grounding, prioritization, actionable CoS judgment, and relationship-state awareness. Current RB can reason, coach, and infer, but canonical RB requires evidence-backed relationship intelligence, persistence, prioritization, orchestration, strategic judgment, and explicit why-it-matters guidance.
